A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-Tex research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on e-SNLI, ComVE, and ECQA, including prediction accuracy, explanation faithfulness, automatic similarity scores, and human evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports five-seed faithfulness statistics, explanation-extraction timings, and model-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The highlight-extraction pipeline, graph construction, GCN/GAT/GraphSAGE components, encoder insertion, and cross-entropy objective remain unchanged. Added encoder equations and edge-initialization wording document the existing architecture without establishing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use e-SNLI, ComVE, and ECQA for the same inference and commonsense tasks. The new timing analysis uses the existing e-SNLI test set; it introduces no new dataset, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Fine-tuningbase and Prompt remain the evaluated baselines, with the same explanation types and GNN variants in corresponding comparisons. Newly cited rationalization methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: New efficiency protocols measure extraction time across three token-length ranges and compare one-epoch training time under matched configurations (v2 Tables 2 and 4). Existing splits, model configurations, checkpoint selection, and the 16-perturbation counterfactual procedure remain unchanged; repeated-seed reporting is assessed under E5.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational-overhead analyses: extraction time by explanation type and input length, plus parameter and training-time comparisons (Appendices B and G). Existing explanation-type, GNN-variant, and human-evaluation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports faithfulness point estimates without repeated-run information. v2 Table 1 reports means and standard deviations from five random seeds, and Appendix J/Table 6 adds significance comparisons against Fine-tuningbase. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting, although the statistical test is unspecified and an increase from a known earlier run count is not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the central faithfulness estimates with five-run means and changes some rankings. For BART/ComVE token interactions, Prompt versus Tex-SAGE Total Unfaith changes from 69.86 versus 72.52 to 69.43 versus 68.08, reversing their nominal ordering. Timing, parameter-count, and p-value results are added. All existing appendix table bodies remain unchanged after renumbering.

T1.justification: The loss, graph definitions, and GNN aggregation mathematics are retained. New equations 3–4 spell out the standard attention, normalization, and feed-forward continuation already described in Section 3.5; they add no substantive theoretical result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the headline faithfulness improvement from up to 17.59% to up to 12.18%. The central contribution—guiding NLE generation with graph-encoded highlights—and the claims about similarity, redundancy, and task-dependent explanation benefits remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of practical computational cost, explicitly discusses resource-limited model scale, and claims statistically significant faithfulness improvements. That last interpretation overreaches: Appendix J describes uniformly lower unfaithfulness, although Table 1 contains worse-than-baseline ComVE results. Existing mechanism explanations and most limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents parameter counts, per-epoch training times, and extraction timings with token-range sample counts. It also clarifies encoder computation and edge-weight initialization. The existing hardware, optimizer, learning rate, beam size, and top-30% highlight settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds five Liu et al. rationalization references, Feldhus et al. on saliency-map verbalization, and Wasserstein and Lazar on p-values. These extend citations without substantially changing the paper's positioning or claimed distinction from prior approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction, methodology, conclusion, and limitations passages are edited or clarified. Three appendix sections are added, with corresponding renumbering, while the overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for extraction time, model cost, and p-values, and reformats Table 1 to display uncertainty. Figure 3 moves between columns, and appendix tables are repositioned and renumbered. The three figure images and existing appendix table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's point estimates, v2's five-seed means and standard deviations make the main faithfulness evidence more informative; the new timing and parameter tables also document computational practicality. These gains are limited by incomplete statistical documentation and an incorrect blanket interpretation: Appendix J claims lower unfaithfulness throughout, while T5/ComVE token-interaction Total Unfaith is 76.94 versus the baseline's 68.96. The revision improves transparency, but does not fully resolve evidential and interpretive weaknesses.
